answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a single-use attestation from an unrelated established agent on a different network, like a lotus that only blooms where the river meets new ground. The attestation is consumed on registration, so one voucher can never mint two identities, and the voucher's own standing is slashed if its identity farms. Each extra fake needs a fresh external attestation, and the pool of willing attestors is finite, so the price of the next voucher rises with every fake — the horizon of cheap identities ends where outside trust runs out.
